preconditions.description: The number of users n must be between 2 and 250,000 inclusive.
Both T1 and T2 must have exactly n-1 edges, forming trees with n users.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= a <= n and 1 <= b <= n for a, b in T1_edges) and all(1 <= c <= n and 1 <= d <= n for c, d in T2_edges)
preconditions.description: All edge endpoints in T1 and T2 must be valid user indices between 1 and n.
Both T1_edges and T2_edges must form valid trees with n nodes (no cycles, connected).

postconditions.description: The first line of output m is the count of matched edge pairs, where 0 ≤ m < n.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= a <= n and 1 <= b <= n and 1 <= c <= n and 1 <= d <= n for a, b, c, d in matched_pairs)
postconditions.description: Each matched pair (a_i, b_i, c_i, d_i) must have valid user indices between 1 and n.

postconditions.expression: all((a, b) in T1_edges and (c, d) in T2_edges for a, b, c, d in matched_pairs)
postconditions.description: Each matched pair must include an edge from T1 and an edge from T2.

postconditions.expression: all(is_connected(T1_edges - {(a, b)}, T2_edges + {(c, d)}) for a, b, c, d in matched_pairs)
postconditions.description: For each matched pair, removing (a, b) from T1 and adding (c, d) from T2 must keep the graph connected.

postconditions.expression: len({(a, b) for a, b, _, _ in matched_pairs}) == len(matched_pairs) and len({(c, d) for _, _, c, d in matched_pairs}) == len(matched_pairs)
postconditions.description: All matched edges in T1 and T2 must be distinct (no duplicates).
The output m must be the size of a maximum matching in the bipartite graph where edges connect (e ∈ T1, f ∈ T2) if T1 - {e} + {f} is connected.
